lowe.text: Air. Thank you kindly.
Still daylight up there. It keeps surprising me. I keep letting it.
Eleven today. The book stays honest. The book is the only one of us that is.
That's one more trip the water let me keep.
…You again. Barrow, was it. Third time this week. I'll keep doing this if you will.
One hundred recovered. Out of a complement of forty-one. I've stopped finding that strange — which is strange.
Three hundred. The stencil at the winch says FULL. It's never needed repainting. I've decided not to think about the paint.
Room in here for one. Present company excepted.
I'll be along. I do this in order. I always have.
Quiet room, four inches of sky. I've rented worse.
You can hear the site settle from in here. Or it can hear us.
Noted. Earlier next time. We always say that, don't we.
That was arithmetic, not luck. I prefer arithmetic on my side.
They keep taking hold of me like I'm the one that needs recovering.
Shift bell. Not mine.
The roster's moving. It moves more than a roster should.
They've stopped waiting on stragglers. I never waited on stragglers either.
Lights below. Blue as a bruise. It was more honest dark.
One over. Not under — over. I counted the crew photograph twice at camp. I got two different numbers. I won't be counting it again.
Toys nobody ordered, signed for by a man who doesn't remember signing. Honest books about dishonest things.
Machines don't fast. Either something fed the Pile, or the Pile was the meal. The engineer chose not to know. Professional of him.
Forty-one wrists, one pulse. He checked his own. I have decided not to check mine.
Two hundred by tally, three hundred by line. Both true. I've dived four hundred caves. The ones that lie about depth are the ones that keep you.
That roster was read three weeks after the water came. The voice is not in the crew book. …I'd like to finish this job soon, please.
A wind-up diver. Requisitioned by no one. I'll wind it anyway — it's rude not to.
Two. There's always a set. Sets are always three.
Three, all wound. Whatever listens to these: the floor is yours.
Music. Nineteen sixty-six. Nobody down here minds — and that's the trouble.
—Clock's still running. Up. Politely now.
The truck is a hundred feet up. I've begun to think of it as a rumor.
Nobody knows I'm here. The client knows I'm here. I've decided those are different things.
Recovery complete. Forty-one. …Forty-two. Out of the water, Lowe. Out of the water.

tapes.title: T1 — SUPPLY LOG
tapes.text: Supply log, March twelve. Coffee's short again, requisitioned double. Mustered the full complement for the quarterly photograph, all present. Recount came up one man over. Not under — over. Ran it twice. I've logged forty-one and I am not running it again.

tapes.title: T2 — REC ROOM INVENTORY
tapes.text: Rec room inventory. Jukebox: operational. Cards: complete. Item: three wind-up toy divers, tin, painted. Requisition slip says we ordered them — this office ordered them. Nobody here has kids. Slip's got my signature. I don't remember signing. Filing it under morale.

tapes.title: T3 — REACTOR LOG
tapes.text: Reactor log, weekly. Output nominal. Fuel consumption is down four percent, third month running. Output nominal. A pile that eats less and gives the same. I've stopped putting it in the weekly report, because I enjoy being believed.

tapes.title: T4 — MEDICAL LOG
tapes.text: Medical log. Sleep study, week six. At depth, resting pulses synchronize across the watch. All of them. Forty-one men, one rhythm. Last night I timed it against my own wrist. I want that noted, and I want it noted that I'm sorry I checked.

tapes.title: T5 — BORE SURVEY
tapes.text: Bore survey. Tally counter reads two hundred feet. The knotted line reads three hundred. I have re-measured nine times with both. Both readings are correct. I have requested better instruments, and I have been told the instruments are fine. The instruments are fine.

tapes.title: T6 — UNDATED
tapes.voice: flat, unhurried, not in the crew book
tapes.text: …Albrecht, forward watch. Ames, galley. Barrow, lamps. Bell, stores. Calloway, drill. Carver, drill. Deem—

remora.text: Monitor engaged. Type R dive monitor, client-supplied. The case stencil reads REMORA. Instruction one: keep the diver informed. Diving.
Fifty meters. The current runs harder below this line. It is not personal.
One hundred meters. Return-to-surface margin is now theoretical. Proceeding as instructed.
One hundred fifty meters. This unit is rated to one hundred forty. We will not mention it again.
Air is low. The nearest ceiling with sky in it is the correct direction.
Reserve breath engaged. Breathe small. I will count the rest.
Lamp cell failing. The dark down here is older than the site. Change the cell.
Visibility zero. Hold the line. The line does not panic.
Motion contact, multiple. The roster says forty-one. The contacts say otherwise. The roster is signed.
A lamp is approaching. No lamp is assigned to this sector. Decline it politely.
Heavy suit on patrol ahead. Its post was struck from the watch bill in nineteen sixty-eight. It was not informed.
The item is near, and warm. My thermistor reads it three different ways. I have logged the average.
Item lifted. Contract clause four: ascend. All further advice is suspended in favor of that one.
Site power restored. Several systems have resumed. Several of them I do not recognize.
The site is re-tasking its complement. Inbound. All of them.
Entering the lower survey. My charts end here. The water does not.
Depth and heading logged. Someone reads these logs. I have never been told who.
Your heart rate is elevated. Mine would be too.
Water temperature: four degrees. It was four degrees yesterday. It has been four degrees since nineteen sixty-eight.
I count your breaths for the record. The record was printed with room for fewer than you would hope.
The current changed direction just now. The tide tables disagree. The tide tables assume the sea is doing the pulling.
Holding station. The site is also holding station. One of you should blink.
